subject: Operational boundary letter request — VPC-managed infrastructure and SLA attribution
thread_content:
From: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@harbortech.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+procurement@harbortech.com
Date: Sat, 30 Sep 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: operational boundary letter for HarborTech VPC dependencies

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. To move forward we need a short, formal statement from Redwood that acknowledges our deployment model and the resulting SLO attribution rules. HarborTech runs Redwood Private inside our VPC (Transit GW + customer-managed firewalls + provider-managed compute). We operate our egress/ingress and the majority of network infrastructure.

Specifically we need Redwood to:
- Acknowledge that latency and availability incidents attributable to our customer-controlled network (transit gateway outages, customer firewall rule misconfiguration, ISP last-mile) are out of scope for Redwood uptime/latency credits.
- Describe how Redwood will attribute latency tails and what visibility you require from us (metrics, syslog, packet capture windows).
- Provide suggested amendment language we can include in the MSA procurement packet.

Can you send a one-page "operational boundary letter" or a short amendment draft we can share with procurement/legal? We've attached a short topology diagram to this thread.

Thanks,
Lina Ortiz
Procurement Lead, HarborTech
---
HarborTech | lina.ortiz@harbortech.com

-----Original Attachment: harbortech-arch-diagram.png (image/png)

---

-----
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@harbortech.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 30 Sep 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operational boundary letter for HarborTech VPC dependencies

Lina — thanks for the clear ask and the diagram. We can provide a concise amendment and an accompanying note on attribution methodology.

Attached: a draft amendment (proposed-amendment-draft.pdf) and a short measurement playbook (measurement-playbook.xlsx) that describes the signals we use to attribute latency and availability to Redwood-hosted runtime vs. customer-managed network. High level:
- Redwood will accept responsibility for latency/availability for failures within our managed stack (runtime, model-serving fabric, routing inside Redwood control plane).
- Incidents caused by customer-managed network elements (transit GW, on-prem-to-cloud VPN, customer NAT/firewall, ISP) will be excluded from uptime and latency credit calculations unless Redwood can independently verify otherwise.
- We require either: (a) customer-provided flow logs and a timestamped traceroute/packet capture window for the incident window, or (b) joint post-incident triage with HarborTech network ops that establishes root cause.

Proposed next steps:
1) Review the attached amendment wording — if it looks good, we can prepare a short appendix for your MSA.
2) Schedule a 60-minute working session this week with your network engineering to go over the measurement playbook and confirm log/metric export formats.
3) If procurement/legal wants tighter wording we can iterate; our legal team prefers a short exclusion clause plus an evidence-based attribution process (rather than blanket exclusions).

I'll set up a calendar invite when I hear your availability.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sophia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0194
Attachment: proposed-amendment-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

-----
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 30 Sep 2028 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operational boundary letter for HarborTech VPC dependencies

Quick internal note —
- Security: we'll need to confirm the types of logs HarborTech is willing to share. Flow logs and timestamped traceroutes are generally OK; we should avoid requesting full packet captures unless there's a signed NDA addendum.
- Legal / contracts: Marissa, please flag if the draft amendment is too permissive or if we should include a short term SLA trial with monitoring obligations.
- Operations: Jonas, can you review the measurement-playbook and confirm whether the evidence we ask for is sufficient to attribute a latency tail to customer infra?

I'll wait for your guidance before sending anything to legal.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 30 Sep 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operational boundary letter for HarborTech VPC dependencies

Thanks — I reviewed the draft. A couple of redlines we should consider:
- Replace any language that says "out of scope" with "attribution-based exclusion" to keep the door open for joint verification.
- Add a clause that requires HarborTech to maintain network health metrics (flow logs, BGP announcements if applicable) for 90 days for auditability.
- For procurement, they may ask for specific credits: propose we offer a limited credit schedule tied to verified Redwood-side failures and exclude verified customer-network failures; sample credit math included in the attached PDF.

I can review the final language with Legal Monday morning unless Procurement needs it earlier.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

-----
From: James Cole <james.cole@harbortech.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@harbortech.com>
Cc: ops+procurement@harbortech.com
Date: Sat, 30 Sep 2028 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operational boundary letter for HarborTech VPC dependencies

Sofia / Team —
Thanks for the quick turnaround and detailed draft. Our network team reviewed the measurement playbook and provided a small tweak: HarborTech is comfortable sharing VPC flow logs and traceroutes; we cannot share packet captures without a separate NDA. We also prefer the phrase "attribution-based exclusion" as Marissa suggested.

I've uploaded an updated topology (harbortech-arch-diagram.png) and a short note with the change request: replace paragraph 3 of the draft with: "Customer-managed network elements (Transit Gateway, customer firewalls, ISP last-mile) are excluded from Redwood uptime and latency credits unless joint post-incident verification attributes the root cause to Redwood-managed systems. Customer will make flow logs and traceroutes available for the incident window upon request."

If that wording works we can move this into procurement and ask for a short joint triage SLA (48 hours to start joint investigation).

Let us know availability for a 60-minute working session tomorrow.

Regards,
James Cole
Director, Infrastructure Operations — HarborTech

-----
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: James Cole <james.cole@harbortech.com>, Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@harbortech.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 30 Sep 2028 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operational boundary letter for HarborTech VPC dependencies

James/Lina — appreciated. We're aligned on the "attribution-based exclusion" phrasing; Marissa's suggested 90-day metrics retention is reasonable and we'll propose that to procurement as an appendix.

Next steps I will take:
- Update the amendment draft to use the new phrasing and add the proposed metrics retention clause (90 days).
- Draft a short paragraph describing the joint triage SLA (proposed 48-hour window to begin investigation and 14-day target for initial RCA).
- Schedule the 60-minute working session — I'm available tomorrow 10:00-11:30 PT or Monday 09:00-12:00 PT.

If HarborTech confirms tomorrow 10:00 PT I'll send an invite and attach the updated amendment.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0194
